criteria: A build that applies `asset/base64` and writes with a CSS-family variable format (`scss/variables`, `css/variables`, `less/variables`, `stylus/variables`) emits each base64 asset value as a double-quoted string literal, e.g. `$asset-icon-delete: "PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0...";`
The generated stylesheet compiles without errors when the base64 value contains `+`, `/`, or `=` padding characters, and the compiled value is the full base64 string, unchanged
Asset values that already contain their own quoting or a CSS function (for example a value produced by `asset/url`) are emitted unchanged and are not wrapped in a second set of quotes

JSON and JavaScript outputs for the same tokens (e.g. `json/flat`, `javascript/es6`) still contain the raw base64 with no surrounding quote characters, so `data:image/png;base64,${token}`-style embedding keeps working
Tokens that are not of type `asset` are unchanged in CSS-family outputs
description:
When `asset/base64` is applied to a `type: "asset"` token and the result is written with a CSS-family variable format (`scss/variables`, `css/variables`, `less/variables`, `stylus/variables`), the value is emitted unquoted:

```scss
$asset-icon-delete: PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0...;
```

Base64 output routinely contains `+`, `/` and `=` padding. In SCSS/Sass those are read as arithmetic/division operators or as a parse error, so the generated stylesheet either fails to compile or silently evaluates to the wrong value. This affects the documented base64-embed workflow (the `assets-base64-embed` example uses exactly this transform + format combination).

The repository's own documentation sets the opposite expectation: the predefined-transforms reference and the `assets-base64-embed` example README both show the output as a double-quoted string, e.g. `$asset-icon-alert-circle: "PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0...";`.

Expected behavior: base64 asset values are emitted as double-quoted string literals in CSS-family outputs, so the generated stylesheet compiles and consumers receive the base64 payload verbatim.

Root cause: the base64 transform returns a bare string and the CSS-family variable formatters append token values verbatim, so nothing in the pipeline adds the quotes the docs describe. Quoting of `asset` tokens was intentionally removed in v4 (replaced by the `asset/url` transform), which left base64 values with no built-in quoting path.

notes:
Scope boundary: do not globally re-introduce double-quoting for all `asset` tokens. The v4 migration guide documents that as a deliberate removal, with `asset/url` as the sanctioned quoting transform; a blanket re-quote would double-quote `url(...)` values and break that path. Quoting must be specific to the base64 string value produced by `asset/base64` in CSS-family outputs.

Do not add quotes inside the `asset/base64` transform unconditionally: `json/flat` (and the JS formats) `JSON.stringify` the token value, so a quoted transform output becomes `"\"PHN2...\""`, breaking the base64 embedding shown in the example README (`data:image/png;base64,${asset-image-logo}`).

Repro: `examples/advanced/assets-base64-embed/config.json`, platform `assets/embed/scss` (`transforms: ["attribute/cti", "name/kebab", "asset/base64"]`, `format: "scss/variables"`). Its README already documents the quoted form as the expected result, so it doubles as the acceptance fixture.

The predefined-transforms entry for `asset/base64` (and the matching JSDoc) is a copy-paste of the Objective-C literal transform — it says the value is wrapped in double quotes and prefixed with `@`, which is wrong on both counts. Worth correcting in the same pass.

Existing format tests already compile generated SCSS with the `sass` package (`compileString`), which is a suitable way to demonstrate the compiled-output criterion.
